Introducing psa > What psa Is

What psa Is

psa is a Python-like language with semantics of its own, designed first of all as a tool-calling language for AI. An agent (or a person) writes a small program in a Python-shaped surface — parse a JSON payload, call HTTP services and other tools, transform data, return a structured result — and psa compiles it ahead of time to a native binary. The compiler binary is named psa; source files carry the suffix .psa.

The compile path has one direction and no shortcuts: psa → SLA → SA. psa emits SLA text; the SLA compiler lowers it to SA; the SA Referee verifies ownership and bounds before any code runs. What cannot be proven or supported is refused loudly at compile time — the check is the security gate that generated code usually does not have, and it is also what makes the output fast: no interpreter, no garbage collector, deterministic resource use.

The author surface: what you do not need to know

psa is written under a surface discipline: the author of a psa program does not need to know what a Vec is, what a PsaVal is, what borrowing means, or what Perceus is. Those are implementation concepts of the layers below. The author writes Python-shaped code — def, class, if/elif/else, for, while, try/except, import, indentation blocks, no declaration keywords — and the compiler infers types and ownership. Where inference can prove a static type, the value takes the zero-cost static path; where it cannot, the value is carried by the dynamic layer. Both are psa; which one a given value takes is decided by the code itself, as the next pages state precisely.

What this chapter is, and what the next one is

This chapter is the general account of psa: its semantic stance (the page that says exactly which semantics psa promises, and where), its layered architecture, the two styles a psa program can mix, its source-map work in development, and its measured status and limits. The companion chapter From Python (psa) to SLA is the item-by-item comparison: the same program in psa and in SLA, construct by construct. Read the comparisons under the stance stated here — a side-by-side table shows how a program is written in the two languages, not a promise that the two languages give every construct the same meaning.

Key Points of This Page

  • psa: a Python-like language of its own, built as an AI tool-calling language; .psa source, the psa compiler.
  • Compile path: psa → SLA → SA, verified by the SA Referee before execution; no interpreter, no GC.
  • The author surface hides the machinery: no Vec, PsaVal, borrowing, or Perceus knowledge is required to write psa.
  • This chapter states the semantics and the measured status; the companion chapter does the construct-by-construct comparison.
